question: Does the contrast between national deconcentration and domestic urban concentration occur in each of the four disciplinary domains?
claim: All four pooled domains have declining national Gini trends, while most continuously observed countries have increasing domestic urban Gini trends; their annual trajectories and between-country variation differ.

panels.a: Matched-country domestic Gini trend swarm, with international-domain trend diamonds and domestic medians.
panels.b: Annual international Gini change in four domains.
panels.c: Median domestic Gini changes with between-country IQR.
panels.d-g: Country-level city-count growth versus domestic Gini trend for four domains, with OLS fits and country-bootstrap confidence bands.

data_policy: Sum cleaned event flows across fields within each official domain before recomputing indices. Domestic inflow and outflow strengths are combined before calculation. Use the same 45-country continuous cohort in all four domains and all 28 years. National indices include every country with positive corresponding strength.
preservation: All existing v1/v2/v3 outputs remain unchanged.

export.layout: Three panels above four square association panels; a and d left axes align.

review_risks: A national index and the distribution of individual domestic-country slopes are distinct estimands; identify the diamond and dots explicitly.
Country dots are the same matched countries across domains, not independent replicated observations for a significance test.
Gini reflects the distribution over positive-flow cities; a rising Gini does not imply a rising HHI or a gain by a fixed group of leading cities.
The domestic annual curve is a median of country-specific baseline changes, not the change in a median index and not the median of fitted slopes.
The pointwise IQR is between-country spread, not a confidence interval.

background_grid.placement: Continue both the major-tick intervals and their midpoint guides beyond the outermost labelled ticks, stopping at plot limits. Use display-space intervals on logarithmic axes.
background_grid.boundary_text_policy: No added perimeter. Keep all interior grid guides clear of text and legend footprints.
background_grid.boundary_rule: No added perimeter; continue regular interior major and midpoint grids up to plot limits.

lower_annotation_placement: Spearman coefficients between each domain title and the plot top, outside the grid.
lower_fit_display_policy: Evaluate the original OLS coefficients across the full common x-axis range. Retain confidence bands only within each domain observed x range.
